Devoted
dē-vō´ted
v. (given over irrevocably; rendering Hebrew charam)
From Latin devovere, to vow away. In Leviticus a devoted thing is placed permanently beyond recovery — the strongest form of dedication in the law.

Biblical Definition

To be devoted is to be given over irrevocably. Leviticus is explicit: “No devoted thing, that a man shall devote unto the LORD of all that he hath… shall be sold or redeemed: every devoted thing is most holy unto the LORD” (Lev 27:28). The psalmist prays, “stablish thy word unto thy servant, who is devoted to thy fear” (Psa 119:38). Jericho was devoted, which is why Achan's theft was fatal (Jos 6:17–18 in the same vocabulary).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines devote as to appropriate by vow; to set apart or dedicate by a solemn act; to consecrate; and to give up wholly; to addict, to direct the attention wholly or chiefly.

expand to see more

DEVOTE, v.t. To appropriate by vow; to set apart or dedicate by a solemn act; to consecrate.

2. To give up wholly; to addict; to direct the attention wholly or chiefly.

3. To give up; to resign.

4. To doom; to consign over.

Key Scripture

Lev 27:28 — "Notwithstanding no devoted thing, that a man shall devote unto the LORD of all that he hath, both of man and beast, and of the field of his possession, shall be sold or redeemed: every devoted thing is most holy unto the LORD."

Psa 119:38 — "Stablish thy word unto thy servant, who is devoted to thy fear."

Jos 6:17 — "And the city shall be accursed, even it, and all that are therein, to the LORD: only Rahab the harlot shall live, she and all that are with her in the house, because she hid the messengers that we sent."

Lev 27:29 — "None devoted, which shall be devoted of men, shall be redeemed; but shall surely be put to death."

Modern Corruption

Dedication is treated as renewable enthusiasm, and the law's devoted thing could not be sold, redeemed, or reconsidered.

expand to see more

Leviticus 27:28 sets devotion apart from every other kind of giving: no devoted thing… shall be sold or redeemed: every devoted thing is most holy unto the LORD. Ordinary vows in that chapter could be redeemed by adding a fifth part; a devoted thing could not. It had crossed a line and could not be brought back, which is what made Achan's wedge of gold from devoted Jericho not merely theft but sacrilege.

Psalm 119:38 asks God to establish His word to a servant already described as devoted to thy fear. The devotion comes first and the request follows; the psalmist is not offering dedication in exchange for a promise but asking God to make good on a word to someone already given over. That order — given first, then asking — is the shape of most petitions in the psalm.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew charam (H2763), to devote, ban, utterly destroy; cherem (H2764), a devoted thing — the word behind Jericho's ban.

expand to see more

Hebrew charam (H2763) — to devote irrevocably; Leviticus 27:28-29, Joshua 6:18.

Hebrew cherem (H2764) — devoted thing, ban; Joshua 7:1, 11-13 of Achan's sin.

Hebrew qodesh qodashim — most holy; Leviticus 27:28, the status conferred.

Usage

"“Every devoted thing is most holy unto the LORD” — beyond sale or redemption."

"“Who is devoted to thy fear” — the servant described before the request."

"“Keep yourselves from the accursed thing” — the warning Achan ignored."
